name: MAPPILAPPATTU
description: The competition focuses on the presentation of traditional Mappilappattu in authentic Mappila musical styles (Ishal), with due importance given to the rich Arabi-Malayalam literary tradition. The composition should follow recognized traditional forms and styles such as Kambi, Kazhuth, Vaalkambi, Valummel Kambi, and other established Mappila patterns. The lyrics should reflect the linguistic and literary character of Arabi-Malayalam and should not contradict Islamic values or demean the cultural heritage of the Mappila tradition. The piece need not be an old or historically known composition; newly written compositions are also permitted, provided they preserve the essential characteristics of traditional Mappilappattu. Pure Malayalam compositions that do not give due importance to the Arabi-Malayalam tradition will not be considered. The minimum length of the song is up to 3 Stanzas.

description: The competition focuses on the presentation of traditional Mappilappattu in authentic Mappila musical styles (Ishal), with due emphasis on the rich Arabi-Malayalam literary tradition. The lyrics should reflect the linguistic, literary, and cultural character of Arabi-Malayalam and should not contradict Islamic values or undermine the cultural heritage and traditions of Mappilappattu. The performance must contain a minimum of three stanzas. Participants must combine two or more Mappilappattu compositions, presenting them consecutively. When multiple songs are combined, the title/author and traditional tune (Ishal) of each song should be clearly identified before its presentation. K6 BUILDATHON A team-based challenge to develop and deploy an original software solution for a given problem or domain, covering ideation, system design, frontend, backend, database, APIs, testing, security, deployment, and scalability. A team of 3 students is allowed to participate. The problem statement/theme will be provided on the spot. Participants are required to develop their solution using AI tools free or paid versions according to the participants comfort such as Google Antigravity, Codex, Claude, ChatGPT and etc and may use registered laptops. The final submission should include a working prototype/product and a brief presentation or demonstration explaining the idea, functionality, and implementation.

Team Size: 3 students

K7 HARDWARE HACKATHON Hardware Hackathon is a team-based, live challenge in which participants identify a realworld problem and develop a functional hardware prototype using microcontrollers, sensors, electronics, embedded systems, and related technologies. Each institution must first submit a project proposal outlining the identified problem, objectives, purpose, proposed solution, work plan, final product, practical application, and a precise inventory of all tools, components, and technologies required. Following proposal approval, the listed components and tools must be presented and sealed prior to the competition to ensure transparency and independent development. During the continuous 6-hour live hackathon, teams will build and demonstrate their proposed prototype using only the approved resources. Projects will be evaluated on innovation, problem relevance, technical integration, functionality, reliability, practical usability, and quality of live implementation. The final submission should include a working prototype/product and a brief presentation or demonstration explaining the idea, functionality, and implementation. PPT including the workflow for the presentation should be created within the above-mentioned time.

K9 COMIC BOOK To create an original comic book in Malayalam language based on a theme given, combining storytelling, character development, dialogue, illustration and visual sequencing. The comic should communicate a complete story through a creative combination of panels, artwork, expressions, narration and dialogue, with emphasis on originality and visual storytelling. The work should contain 10-15 A4 pages, including the front and back covers, and may be created through hand-drawing or digital illustration. The completed comic should present a coherent beginning, development and conclusion.

K10 PODCAST A group of three members (mandatory) should participate, with additional members allowed, to produce a podcast in Malayalam language on a given theme consisting of one episode lasting 15 minutes. The podcast should present a meaningful discussion around the theme, featuring fresh, original content that has not been previously published. Involvement of non-students in this item is not allowed. Engage storytelling with highquality content. The team’s ability to create compelling and informative video content is considered.

Team Size: 3 students K11 HERITAGE DOCUMENTARY Heritage Documentary is a 6–8-minute, research-based Malayalam documentary competition that challenges participants to explore and creatively present a significant aspect of a heritage through original research, on-screen presentation, narration, and purposeful visual storytelling. A strong preference will be given to documentaries featuring the participating students themselves through direct-to-camera narration and field-based documentation, supported by original footage, interviews, archival materials, photographs, maps, graphics, and relevant B-roll. Every visual and narrative element should meaningfully contribute to the central story, with historical and cultural claims grounded in reliable sources and external materials appropriately credited. The competition values authenticity, research depth, originality, storytelling, factual accuracy, visual coherence, and production quality, while encouraging participants to explore the significance, evolution, and contemporary relevance of heritage. The Proposal should be submitted and approved.

K12 FONT CREATION An innovative Arts Fest event that challenges students to create an original visual style for Malayalam letters. Participants will design a consistent set of Malayalam letterforms, demonstrate creativity while preserving readability and the identity of the script. The focus is on developing a typeface system, not merely decorating individual letters. Design Workflow: Participants can use tools such as Adobe Illustrator, CorelDRAW, Glyphrstudio or FontForge to design and generate a functional Unicode-compatible Malayalam font. Submission Requirements: • Submit the completed font in TTF format. • Include the original editable source file (AI, CDR, or equivalent). • Ensure proper character mapping, spacing, readability, and support for essential Malayalam characters, vowel signs, chillaksharams, and conjunct letters. • The font must be original and function correctly in compatible digital applications. • Include complete font branding assets (such as a brand identity guide, showcase poster, or specimen sheet) packaged together with the font and source files as a ZIP archive. name: PROUD MUSLIM
description: Proud Muslim is designed to identify students who demonstrate strong intellectual understanding of Islamic principles and the ability to articulate, defend, and critically engage with contemporary issues from an Islamic perspective. The competition will be conducted in two phases in Malayalam language. Phase 01 – Written Elimination Round This is an offstage written examination. The questions will cover contemporary intellectual and ideological issues such as Atheism, New Atheism, Modernism, Liberalism, Feminism, LGBTQ+ Politics, Theology, the Modern Self, and Gender and Sexuality in Islam. First phase will be conducted along with non-stage programmes. Phase 02 – Personal Debate The candidates will participate in a personal debate. Each candidate will be provided with four topics 24 hours before the programme. Candidates must prepare all four topics in advance. Two hours before their respective presentation, the specific topic to be presented by each candidate will be determined through a controlled draw. Each candidate will be given 4 minutes to present and defend their position on the selected topic. This will be followed by a 4-minute question-and-answer segment. During this segment, the other three candidates and the judges will ask questions related to the presented topic. Each question will be given 15 seconds, and the presenting candidate will have 45 seconds to respond. The same process will be repeated for each candidate in turn. The final winner will be determined based on the candidate’s depth of knowledge, intellectual clarity, quality of argumentation, ability to defend their position, critical thinking, and effectiveness in responding to questions. The final result will be based on the marks scored in both phases.

name: HERITAGE DOCUMENTARY
description: Heritage Documentary is a 6–8 minute, research-based documentary competition that challenges participants to explore and creatively present a significant aspect of a heritage through original research, on-screen presentation, narration, and purposeful visual storytelling. A strong preference will be given to documentaries featuring the participating students themselves through direct-to-camera narration and field-based documentation, supported by original footage, interviews, archival materials, photographs, maps, graphics, and relevant B-roll. Every visual and narrative element should meaningfully contribute to the central story, with historical and cultural claims grounded in reliable sources and external materials appropriately credited. The competition values authenticity, research depth, originality, storytelling, factual accuracy, visual coherence, and production quality, while encouraging participants to explore the significance, evolution, and contemporary relevance of heritage. The Proposal should be submitted and approved.
